categories.main_business_segments: Tsukishima Holdings operates two main business segments: the Water Environment Business, which focuses on water and sewage treatment plants, sludge recycling, and biomass utilization facilities; and the Industrial Business, which provides industrial infrastructure for the chemical, life sciences, and secondary battery sectors, as well as environmental equipment for waste and effluent treatment. There is also a minor 'Other' segment, primarily involving real estate management and printing services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include advanced water and sewage treatment processes, sludge dehydration, drying, and incineration systems, as well as crystallization, filtration, centrifugation, and drying technologies for industrial applications. They emphasize energy-efficient and high-performance equipment, such as next-generation incinerators, membrane bioreactors, and ultra-fine particle crystallization devices. R&D also focuses on integrating AI, ICT, and simulation for process optimization and automation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers for the Water Environment Business are Japanese local governments and public sector entities responsible for water infrastructure. The Industrial Business serves chemical manufacturers, life sciences (cosmetics, food, pharmaceuticals), secondary battery producers (notably for EVs), and companies requiring waste and effluent treatment. The company also engages in public-private partnership (PPP) projects and provides after-sales maintenance and operation services.
categories.geographic_coverage: Tsukishima Holdings’ primary market is Japan, which accounts for the vast majority of sales. The company also has a presence in Asia (notably Thailand, China, Malaysia, and Taiwan) and some activities in Europe (Germany) through subsidiaries and joint ventures. Overseas sales represent a small but growing portion of total revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates as a midstream and downstream player, providing engineering, procurement, construction (EPC), and operation & maintenance (O&M) services for water and industrial infrastructure. It supplies both turnkey plants and standalone equipment, and is involved in long-term facility management and public-private partnership projects.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding business domains, strengthening group profitability, and promoting sustainability management. R&D focuses on decarbonization (e.g., sludge-to-energy, lithium-ion battery materials), resource recycling, digital transformation (DX), and next-generation energy technologies such as ammonia utilization. The company is also pursuing M&A, alliances, and open innovation with universities to enhance technological capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through project-based sales of plants and equipment, long-term operation and maintenance contracts, and public-private partnership (PFI/DBO) projects. Additional income comes from real estate leasing and printing services. The company also receives management fees and dividends from subsidiaries as a holding company.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In the water environment sector, major competitors include large engineering firms such as JFE Engineering and Metawater. Tsukishima Holdings has established a leading position in Japan’s water and sludge treatment market, especially after integrating JFE’s domestic water engineering business. In industrial equipment, it competes with specialized machinery and process engineering firms, maintaining a strong niche in crystallization and separation technologies.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales reached ¥139.2 billion (approx. $900 million), with operating profit of ¥8.9 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥6.7 billion. The company has demonstrated strong growth, with sales and profits reaching record highs, and targets further expansion to ¥160 billion in sales and ¥12 billion in operating profit by FY2027. The group employs over 3,500 people.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Tsukishima Holdings differentiates itself through advanced environmental and process technologies, comprehensive lifecycle solutions (from design and construction to long-term O&M), and a strong track record in public-private partnerships. The company emphasizes its contribution to decarbonization, resource recycling, and sustainable infrastructure, positioning itself as a technology leader and trusted partner for both public and industrial clients.
